traits: The rhythms of the song and the sword both call to Elena and she will face down anyone who stands her way of perfecting either.
[Coins (for the Ferryman)]: Once per session, activate your Virtue to take your first Action before anyone else in a round.
[Coins (for the Ferryman)]: Once per session, you receive a hero point when you refuse to leave well enough alone or quit while you’re ahead, and it gets you into trouble.
[Quirk]: Earn a hero point when you use your crowd-pleasing skills for something more than making a few coins.
[Quirk]: Earn a hero point when you resort to the edge of your blade to defend a noble ideal.
Choose a specific Performance type, such as singing, playing a specific musical instrument, or dancing. You gain your Virtuoso die when you Perform using that art.

Spend a hero point to convince another character to grant you an object you want at no cost. They might give you something they already have or go to some lengths—legal or illegal—to procure the item, whatever is the easiest way for them to get their hands on what you want.
You may choose a Dueling Style. If you purchase this Advantage again, you gain an additional Dueling Style. See the Dueling chapter for more information.

Spend a hero point to convince a Villain you are on her side. The Villain considers you a trusted ally. As soon as the Villain sees you perform a Heroic action or if you refuse to perform a Villainous action, the illusion is over. You can only use this Advantage on each Villain once. “Fool me once…”
Alcohol never adversely affects you, no matter how much you drink.

While aboard a ship, treacherous footing never affects you. You may add your Sea Legs to any physical Test while aboard a ship at sea—engaging in a sword fight on a pitching ship deck, or climbing through the rigging during a storm.
When armed with the signature weapons of any of your styles, you may add your Duelist die to any combat-related test.
(Each additional style learned will increase your Duelist die by one step, to a maximum of d12.)

Originally developed for bullfighting, the Torres style makes use of a rapier in one hand and a cloak in the other. The student uses subtle movements to draw her opponent’s attention to the cloak, and then blindside them with the rapier.

The Torres school is an extremely effective defensive style, as the cloak and sword combine to form a wall of cloth and steel between the student and her opponent’s blade. Masters of the school are some of the most quick-witted and agile men and women in the world.
[Signature Weapons] Wielding a fencing sword (such as a rapier or cutlass) in one hand and nothing in the other, and wearing a long cloak.
[Matador’s Flourish] Spend a hero point to prevent any combat-related wound or injury up to your Athletics (d10).
